_note: Placement map for room 4 (Dining), first floor, level 1 -- ROUND 2. All coordinates are ROOM-LOCAL feet from the footprint's min corner: exactly what roomkit.place takes. Every piece is authored DIRECTLY in room-local coordinates and placed at rot 0; `pos` is the model bbox centre in x/z with pos.y = the height its min-Y sits at, so `pos` is a bbox artefact, not a design number. Build scripts live in scratchpad/dbuild/ (dcommon.py + p_*.py, each idempotent by piece name). Read tools/roomkit/ROOM-BRIEF.md first.
_round2: The footprint was RE-TRACED under round 1: the room went from a 19 x 17 rect to a 14.64 x 13.12 POLYGON with a three-facet BAY on the WEST wall, and its anchor moved (+5.31, -3.80). Every piece was rebuilt from scratch. Round 1's biggest stated limitation is gone -- the bay is real geometry now and its three windows sit on the canted facets. Round 1's painted 'cased reveals' are gone too: both doorways are real cut openings. Round 1's per-wall emissive wall skin ('Dining Walls') and its emissive trim are DELETED -- daylight.js was fixed app-wide between rounds and a critic rejected emissive runs for glowing as bright fins.

_room.name: Dining
_room.bay: WEST wall, three facets, protruding 2.28 ft: canted 9.60->8.44, flat face x=0 from z 3.84..8.44, canted 3.84->2.68. Same shape and depth as the Kitchen's (room 6) bay one room north.

_orientation.verdict: Round 1 had the orientation RIGHT. It was re-derived from scratch this round because a sibling room was found 180 degrees out, and it survived every check.
_orientation.how_it_was_derived: 1) WORLD RECTS (roomkit.rooms --list + the rooms table): Frontyard is z 35..43, i.e. +Z is the FRONT of the house, and Dining's south wall at world z 34.82 abuts it. Kitchen (room 6) is x -4.19..10.68, z 4.74..21.48 -- directly NORTH. First floor hallway (room 12, which holds the staircase) is x 10.70..18.30 -- directly EAST. 2) FLOOR PLAN (docs/floor plan/Main Floor Plan App.png): the plan is drawn front-at-top with the garage on the left, so plan-up = +world z and plan-right = -world x. The bay notch on the plan is on the plan-RIGHT edge of the Dining outline = world WEST, at plan y matching world z 24.9..30.6 -- within half a foot of the traced polygon's 24.38..31.30. 3) PHOTOS: photo B looks straight down the table at the bay with the CLOCK wall on the left and the BUFFET wall on the right, which only works if clock=SOUTH and buffet=NORTH; photo C (facing north) shows the kitchen through a wide opening on the LEFT of the buffet wall and the STAIRCASE through a second opening on the right, matching kitchen=north-west-end and hallway=east; photo f (facing south) shows the foyer's white door on the far LEFT and the bay on the far RIGHT, i.e. east=left, west=right.

_orientation.south_z13_12: front facade -- window / round clock / window
_orientation.west_bay: side facade -- the three-facet bay, one window per facet

_openings.note: house.js buildRoom cuts a REAL hole per row. A 'passage' gets NO panel at all; a 'window' gets the app's translucent glass pane -- so p_windows.py deliberately builds no glass sheet of its own (an opaque one hid the view bands and made every raised blind read as a pale slab).
list: edge 6 off 0.30 w 3.00 y 0.00 h 7.20 passage -- to the KITCHEN. Set to the SAME world span room 6 already cut on its own side (its edge 0, offset 9.29, width 3.00 -> world x -1.61..1.39); both rooms are anchored at world x -4.19 so the local numbers match one for one. A mismatched pair would show the neighbour's jamb lining floating inside our hole.
edge 7 off 1.00 w 5.60 y 0.00 h 7.20 passage -- to the HALLWAY/staircase. The stairs trace to world z 23..30 on the plan = local z 1.3..8.3, which is what this opening faces.
edge 0 off 1.88 w 2.60 y 3.00 h 4.25 window -- front facade, east (centre local x 11.46)
edge 0 off 7.88 w 2.60 y 3.00 h 4.25 window -- front facade, west (centre local x 5.46); the clock hangs between them at x 8.46
edge 2 off 0.55 w 1.46 y 3.00 h 4.25 window -- bay, south facet

_camera.primary: custom -- pos [7.61,14.30,22.70] target [1.81,9.60,34.30] fov 100, 900x1200. Matched to Dining A.jpg: the photo is an ultra-wide from beside the buffet's east end looking south-south-west, which puts the foyer opening at the far left, the clock centre, the bay right and the buffet's near end wrapped into the bottom corner. None of the canned poses is wide enough for that; corner_ne is the closest but frames only the table.
_camera.also_good: look_n (buffet/TV wall + the kitchen through the real opening), plan (proves the ceiling is invisible from above)
_camera.warning: the shot's zoom is NOT reproducible run to run -- scene.js lerps the camera distance back toward its zoom target after flyTo. Framing differences between rounds are that, not a moved piece.

_dollhouse_quadrant.why: All four quadrants were reasoned through and two were rendered. doll_ne is unusable for THIS room for a reason that has nothing to do with the room: the KITCHEN's own 9 ft south wall stands between a north-east camera and us, and at the doll pose's 57 degree pitch it eats the northern ~5.9 ft of our floor -- the entire buffet and TV wall disappears. doll_sw and doll_nw both cull the west wall, which throws the bay's three window units into mid-air, and the bay is the room's signature. doll_se culls SOUTH + EAST: the buffet, the TV and the whole bay all stay backed, and what is lost is the south wall, whose window casings, blinds, baseboard and crown are all placed objects that are never culled -- so a white trim outline still stands there and the cutaway reads. The one visible cost is the round clock, which hangs with no wall behind it; from this angle it is seen nearly edge-on and reads as a dark disc rather than an error.

Dining Floor.note: UNPICKABLE by name. Three layers, all tone fields rasterised through kraster.raster (scratchpad/kbuild/kraster.py): (a) the wall-to-wall CARPET as a 10-tone loop-pile field over the app slab at y 0.030 -- the slab alone renders essentially flat and photo A's carpet measures sd 16.2; (b) the area RUG at y 0.052, 10.4 x 8.8 ft over x 2.45..12.85 / z 2.45..11.25, a 12-tone basket-weave lattice with a proud binding band; (c) EVERY contact shadow in the room at y 0.064. The shadows are ONE smooth exponential distance field in TRANSLUCENT tones -- table pool + a tight one under each pedestal, all eight chairs, the buffet, the side table and both plants. No rings, no nested rectangles: round 2 of two sibling rooms shipped concentric bands and both critics called them bullseye decals.

Dining Ceiling.note: UNPICKABLE. Tray ceiling: perimeter soffit at 8.16, recess panel at 8.96, risers + applied moulding between. THE OUTLINE IS NOT A RECTANGLE -- round 1's open item. Photos B and f both show the recess stepping OUT toward the bay in the middle of the west side and stepping back at both ends, so the recess is x 4.30..12.64 / z 2.05..11.07 PLUS a bump to x 2.10 over z 4.30..8.00. Ceiling medallion under the chandelier, round supply diffuser at (4.55, 3.30). Every horizontal face is ONE-SIDED and faces DOWN: solid at eye level, invisible from the plan pose. The ceiling is the ONLY emissive-driven surface in the room -- a downward face collects ~0.05 of scene radiance here, so with none it renders as a black lid.

Dining Crown.note: UNPICKABLE. Built-up crown springing from the wall at 7.40 and dying into the tray soffit at 8.16, 0.545 ft projection, THREE members. It was five at first and read as horizontal siding from below because every step edge catches the sun as its own line. Unbroken all the way round: both cased openings stop at 7.20 and every window head at 7.25. NO EMISSIVE.

Dining Baseboards.note: UNPICKABLE. The whole lower-wall trim programme: baseboard 0..0.60 with a proud cap, chair rail 2.70..2.92 with a cap the window stools land on, and picture-frame wainscot mouldings 0.78..2.56 in 0.155 ft stock, auto-fitted ~2.5 ft wide with 0.52 ft gaps into every wall run. Broken only at the two cased openings. NO EMISSIVE.

Dining Openings.note: The jamb/head linings and flat casing for the two REAL cased openings. The linings run AWAY from the room into the wall cavity so the casing stays flush with the wall plane and lands on the baseboard; the reveal's depth comes from albedo (TRIM_LO a few steps below TRIM) because this renderer has no shadows.

Dining Windows.note: All five units in one model, each on its real hole: two on the front facade and one on EACH BAY FACET, canted with the wall. Per unit: jamb lining, a stool sitting on the chair-rail cap (the photos show no apron -- the rail does that job), flat casing with a head cap, sash frame + meeting rail + centre mullion on the wide units, and white 2 in faux-wood blinds RAISED to half-mast with the slats tilted 30 deg open, which is what photo A shows. Below the blinds, four emissive bands 0.28 ft outside the hole read as sky / treeline / the neighbour's porch rail / lawn -- that light is most of what photo A is, and without it the hole shows the app's single-floor studio backdrop.

Dining Table.note: Espresso plank-top table on twin block pedestals at x +/- 1.85 from centre, long axis EAST-WEST (photo B looks straight down its length at the bay). Centre (7.10, 6.90): x is the room centre, z is pushed 0.3 ft south of it because the photos show the buffet side tight and the front-wall side open. SEE _does_the_table_fit.

Dining Chairs.note: All eight parsons chairs in ONE model so they never drift out of register with the table: 3 + 3 on the long sides at 2.50 ft spacing, 1 at each end. Linen seat 1.62 x 1.60 at 1.45 ft, a rounded reclined back to 3.42 ft with a rolled crown, four tapered espresso posts. The WEST end chair stands in the bay mouth (x centre 2.56, back to x 1.58) -- that is where photo B puts it and the bay's flat face is 4.60 ft wide at that z, so it fits. Rebuild after moving the table: positions derive from TABLE_C in dcommon.py.

Dining Table Decor.note: The clutter photos A/B/f actually show: two dark oval placemats, a white tray with a paper-towel roll on a chrome post and two wood-lidded glass canisters, a glass caddy of odds and ends, a cardboard parcel, a padded envelope, a dark bowl and a phone. Every room judged so far lost points for being tidier than its photo.

Dining Chandelier.note: Black six-arm fixture, 1.06 ft arm radius, frosted cylinder shades standing on the arms. Shade bottoms ~2.9 ft above the table top. Chain + rod up to a canopy at the tray recess (8.96), meeting the ceiling medallion.

Dining Clock.note: 2.30 ft round wall clock centred between the two front-facade windows at x 8.46, centre 5.55 ft up: thin black rim, black Roman ticks and hands over a planked natural-wood face. Depth matters -- INTO the room is -z on this wall, and the first pass had the rim in front of the planks, which rendered the whole thing as a black bulge.

Dining Buffet.note: Black sideboard against the north wall, 5.2 x 2.92 ft high x 1.72 deep, eight fronts on a 4 x 2 grid with slim black bar pulls, on a recessed plinth. The carcase is a darker black than the door faces so the reveals read -- at one tone the whole piece rendered as an undifferentiated black mass. On top (photo C): the deep-red rose dome in a dark footed vessel, a black drip coffee machine, a white tray, a leaning framed print.

Dining TV.note: Framed flat panel over the buffet, bottom at 4.36 ft. The white frame is a BORDER, not a slab: a full rectangle in front of the screen renders as a blank white panel.

Dining Side Table.note: The little black side table standing between the dining table's east end and the buffet in photo B, with a stack of mail and a dark box on it.

Dining Fig Tree.note: Fiddle-leaf fig on a black three-leg stand in a white pot, in the corner where the front wall meets the bay -- where photos A and f put it. 42 violin leaves on short branches off a woody trunk, crown 3.2 to 6.9 ft (clear of the crown at 7.40). Position was pulled in from the hard corner twice: the foliage was poking through the west wall at x 2.28.

Dining Snake Plant.note: Snake plant in a white pot standing just south of the foyer opening, the one at the left edge of photo f. 24 tapered blades.

Dining Vents.note: The dark floor register near the front wall (photo B) and the white wall register on the short west wall segment (photo f, bottom right).

_does_the_table_fit.question: The re-trace cost the room 4.4 x 3.9 ft. Does the real 8 ft table with eight chairs still fit?
_does_the_table_fit.answer: YES, at 7.80 x 3.80 ft, which is within the read of the photos rather than a silent shrink. Photo B shows three parsons chairs a side; three chairs at 2.50 ft spacing need 7.5 ft of table plus overhang, so the real top is 7.5-8.0 ft and 7.80 sits in that band. The measurements: the table spans x 3.20..11.00 and z 5.00..8.80. West end chair 1.58..3.38 -- it sits in the BAY MOUTH, which is 4.60 ft wide over z 3.84..8.44 and easily holds the chair's 1.62 ft width. East end chair 10.82..12.62, leaving 2.02 ft to the east wall. North side chairs reach back to z 3.38, and the buffet is 1.72 ft deep, so the walk-through on the buffet side is 1.66 ft -- tight, and tight is exactly what photos B and C show. South side chairs reach z 10.42, leaving 2.70 ft to the front wall, which is the open side in photo f. At a full 8.0 ft the end clearances drop to ~1.9 ft and it still fits; nothing had to be shrunk to make the room work.

_surfaces.note: wall_color is picked so the room's AVERAGE wall lands near the photo rather than tuning to one wall -- see _tone. floor_color barely shows now (Dining Floor lays a carpet tone field over the slab) but it is set to the field's mean so any sliver at a wall line matches.

_tone.empty_room_meter: roomkit.meter 4 --level 1, AFTER the app-level daylight fix and with round 1's emissive skin deleted: north 226 / west 185 / east 149 / south 122, spread 104 bytes. That spread is the renderer's one-sun-no-bounce limit (ROOM-BRIEF 'a known limit, not your bug'), and it was NOT fought with emissive this round.
_tone.note: The carpet was deliberately aimed at photo A's value AND close to its spread. It went 185/sd 39 -> 141/sd 23 over three passes; overshooting the spread to a light/dark patchwork is a documented sibling failure, so it was pulled back rather than pushed further. The table top is ~35 bytes brighter than photo A's -- photo A is a strongly backlit exposure and photo f measures the same wood at 106, which is where the render sits.

_gaps: The table top renders ~95 against photo A's 61. Photo A is backlit and photo f puts the same wood at 106; the render is between them, closer to f.
The carpet field's spread is 23 against the photo's 16. Reducing it further starts to read as plastic, which is the failure mode on the other side.

In the doll_se dollhouse pose the south wall is culled and the round clock hangs with no wall behind it. That is inherent to a cutaway of a wall that carries art; the alternative quadrants cost either the bay or the whole buffet wall (see _dollhouse_quadrant).
doll_ne is unusable here because the Kitchen's own 9 ft south wall occludes the northern ~6 ft of this room's floor at that pitch. Nothing inside room 4 can fix that.

The window 'view' is four flat emissive bands, not real scenery. At night they stay bright, as does the ceiling -- the same trade-off the master bedroom's ceiling has, and the only emissive left in this room.
Chair fabric is flat colour; the photo's linen has a visible grain. The rug's basket weave is a tone lattice rather than real loop geometry.
No outlet or switch plates, and the framed print on the buffet is a plain rectangle rather than the photo's actual image.
